mechanism.name: Extreme quantile with a tail-dependent Cauchy auxiliary variable
generation_equations: (V,U) has the bivariate standard Cauchy law restricted to V>0,U>0, with scale matrix I_2 (source s=0).
Equivalent independent-normal construction: G0,G1,G2 iid N(0,1), V=abs(G1)/abs(G0), U=abs(G2)/abs(G0).
F_0(v)=2*atan(v)/pi for v>=0. Outcome Y=-log(1-F_0(V)); observed covariate X1=U. Source gamma=0 in equation (16).

Two independent samples from the same population: source_n_labeled rows with observed Y and source_n_unlabeled rows with observed X only. R=1 in the first labeled block; Y_obs=Y there. R=0 in the remaining block; Y_obs=0 is a placeholder.

assumptions: Independent sampling units; labeled and unlabeled samples are independent draws from the same joint/marginal population.
Label availability is fixed by sampling design independently of generated values, corresponding to MCAR sampling.
The stated distributions, independence conditions and selected population functional define the target. Its numerical verification applies to the declared scenario.

properties.notes: One auxiliary covariate with infinite first moment; Y has an exponential marginal. Dependence persists even with source s=0. The target density equals 0.002 at the queried quantile. effective_dimension counts inputs that determine the conditional response law, including an observed surrogate or the sole tail-dependent auxiliary variable; correlated extra coordinates may carry additional information. high_dimensional compares total dimension with source labeled sample size. Interactions marks a nonadditive response/probability map.

estimand.name: Q_Y(0.998)
estimand.definition: Marginal quantile inf{y:Pr(Y<=y)>=0.998} in the common population; tail probability is fixed at 0.002.

truth.expression: Marginal quantile inf{y:Pr(Y<=y)>=0.998} in the common population; tail probability is fixed at 0.002.
truth.derivation: The probability integral transform gives Y~Exponential(rate=1). Thus Q_Y(0.998)=-log(0.002). Dependence with X1 is retained by the common denominator.

adaptations: Select s=0,gamma=0,n=500,m=1000 and p=1/500 from the source quantile setting.
Rename source target X as Y and source auxiliary Y as X1 to match the collection schema.
Use the equivalent absolute-normal construction for the s=0 first-quadrant law and evaluate the survival probability with atan2 for tail stability.
Represent independent labeled/unlabeled samples in a single table: all X columns, label indicator R and Y_obs. A zero on an R=0 row is a finite placeholder.
The generate argument n counts total rows. Source total yields exact source allocation; other n use nearest-integer ratio allocation with both groups nonempty.
Use local PCG64 random streams, with independent covariate and response-noise streams. Each row remains an independent population draw.
